sub_obligations.legal_text: Where the icons are presented electronically they shall be machine-readable.
sub_obligations.plain_summary: Privacy icons shown electronically must be readable by software.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only if standardized icons are presented electronically.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: If privacy icons are presented electronically, does the policy state that they are machine-readable?

sub_obligations.legal_text: The Commission shall be empowered to adopt delegated acts in accordance with [Article 92](https://gdpr-info.eu/art-92-gdpr/) for the purpose of determining the information to be presented by the icons and the procedures for providing standardised icons.
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The European Commission is given authority to establish what information standardized privacy icons should show and how those icons should be provided.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy describe any applicable standardized-icon requirements established by the European Commission?

article_name: Information to be provided where personal data are collected from the data subject

sub_obligations.legal_text: the identity and the contact details of the controller and, where applicable, of the controller’s representative;
sub_obligations.plain_summary: When collecting someone's personal information, the privacy notice must identify the organization responsible for it and, where relevant, its representative, with their contact details.

sub_obligations.legal_text: the purposes of the processing for which the personal data are intended

sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when personal information is collected directly from the person.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the privacy notice clearly state the purposes for which the collected personal information will be used?

sub_obligations.legal_text: as well as the legal basis for the processing;
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The privacy notice must explain the legal reason that allows the organization to use the personal information.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when personal information is collected directly from the person.

sub_obligations.legal_text: where the processing is based on point (f) of [Article 6](https://gdpr-info.eu/art-6-gdpr/)(1), the legitimate interests pursued by the controller or by a third party;
sub_obligations.plain_summary: If the organization relies on its own or another party's legitimate interests, the privacy notice must explain what those interests are.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when processing relies on Article 6(1)(f).

sub_obligations.legal_text: the recipients or categories of recipients of the personal data, if any;

sub_obligations.legal_text: or to object to processing

sub_obligations.legal_text: without affecting the lawfulness of processing based on consent before its withdrawal;
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The notice must explain that withdrawing permission does not affect whether earlier consent-based use of the information was lawful.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when processing relies on consent.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Where consent is the legal basis, does the privacy notice explain that withdrawing consent does not affect the lawfulness of earlier processing?

sub_obligations.legal_text: the right to lodge a complaint with a supervisory authority;
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The privacy notice must tell people that they can complain to a privacy regulator.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when personal information was not obtained directly from the person.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the privacy notice tell people that they have the right to complain to a supervisory authority?

sub_obligations.legal_text: from which source the personal data originate
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The privacy notice must tell people where their personal information came from.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when personal information was obtained from another source rather than directly from the person.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the privacy notice identify the source from which the person's personal information was obtained?

sub_obligations.legal_text: and if applicable, whether it came from publicly accessible sources;
sub_obligations.plain_summary: If relevant, the privacy notice must say whether the information came from a source that was publicly accessible.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only where the source of the personal information was publicly accessible.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: If applicable, does the privacy notice state whether the personal information came from a publicly accessible source?

sub_obligations.legal_text: the existence of automated decision-making, including profiling, referred to in [Article 22](https://gdpr-info.eu/art-22-gdpr/)(1) and (4)
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The privacy notice must tell people if decisions about them are made automatically, including through profiling, where covered by Article 22.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when Article 22(1) or 22(4) automated decision-making, including profiling, is used.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: If Article 22 automated decision-making or profiling is used, does the privacy notice clearly state that it exists?

sub_obligations.legal_text: and, at least in those cases, meaningful information about the logic involved
sub_obligations.plain_summary: For covered automated decisions, the privacy notice must give meaningful information about how the decision-making system works.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: At minimum, only where Article 22(1) or 22(4) automated decision-making is used.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: For covered automated decision-making, does the privacy notice provide meaningful information about the logic used to make the decisions?

sub_obligations.legal_text: as well as the significance and the envisaged consequences of such processing for the data subject.
sub_obligations.plain_summary: For covered automated decisions, the privacy notice must explain what the processing means for the person and its expected effects on them.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: At minimum, only where Article 22(1) or 22(4) automated decision-making is used.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: For covered automated decision-making, does the privacy notice explain its significance and expected consequences for the person?

sub_obligations.legal_text: within a reasonable period after obtaining the personal data, but at the latest within one month, having regard to the specific circumstances in which the personal data are processed;
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The required notice must normally be given within a reasonable time after obtaining the information and no later than one month, taking the circumstances into account.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when personal information was not obtained directly from the person and neither of the alternative timing rules in Article 14(3)(b) or (c) applies earlier.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy state that the required notice is provided within a reasonable period after obtaining the information and no later than one month, unless an earlier deadline applies?

sub_obligations.legal_text: if the personal data are to be used for communication with the data subject, at the latest at the time of the first communication to that data subject; or
sub_obligations.plain_summary: If the information will be used to contact the person, the required notice must be given no later than the first contact.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when the obtained personal information will be used to communicate with the person.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: If the obtained information will be used to contact the person, does the policy require the privacy notice to be provided no later than the first communication?

sub_obligations.legal_text: if a disclosure to another recipient is envisaged, at the latest when the personal data are first disclosed.
sub_obligations.plain_summary: If the information will be shared with another recipient, the required notice must be given no later than the first disclosure.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when disclosure of the obtained personal information to another recipient is planned.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: If the information will be disclosed to another recipient, does the policy require the privacy notice to be provided no later than the first disclosure?

sub_obligations.legal_text: Where the controller intends to further process the personal data for a purpose other than that for which the personal data were obtained
sub_obligations.plain_summary: If the organization plans to use obtained personal information for a new purpose, it must provide additional notice before starting that use.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when the organization intends to use the information for a purpose different from the purpose for which it was obtained.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy describe a process for notifying people before their information is used for a purpose different from the original purpose?

sub_obligations.legal_text: the controller shall provide the data subject prior to that further processing with information on that other purpose
sub_obligations.plain_summary: Before starting the new use, the organization must tell the person what the new purpose is.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when further processing for a new purpose is intended.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy state that people will be informed of the new purpose before their information is used for it?

sub_obligations.legal_text: and with any relevant further information as referred to in paragraph 2.
sub_obligations.plain_summary: Before the new use begins, the organization must also provide any other relevant information required under paragraph 2.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when further processing for a new purpose is intended.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy state that people will receive any relevant additional information required under Article 14(2) before the new use begins?

sub_obligations.legal_text: the data subject already has the information;
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The information does not need to be provided again when the person already has it.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when the person already has the required information.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy recognize that repeated notice is unnecessary when the person already has the required information?

sub_obligations.legal_text: the provision of such information proves impossible or would involve a disproportionate effort
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The usual notice requirement may not apply when providing the information is impossible or would require disproportionate effort.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when providing the required information is impossible or would involve disproportionate effort.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy describe when the organization may rely on impossibility or disproportionate effort as a reason not to provide the usual notice?

sub_obligations.legal_text: in particular for processing for archiving purposes in the public interest, scientific or historical research purposes or statistical purposes
sub_obligations.plain_summary: This exception may be particularly relevant when information is used for public-interest archiving, scientific or historical research, or statistics.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when the processing involves public-interest archiving, scientific or historical research, or statistical purposes and the notice requirement is impossible or disproportionate.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: If the organization relies on this exception for archiving, research, or statistical processing, does the policy identify the relevant purpose and explain why providing notice would be impossible or disproportionate?

sub_obligations.legal_text: subject to the conditions and safeguards referred to in [Article 89](https://gdpr-info.eu/art-89-gdpr/)(1)
sub_obligations.plain_summary: When this exception is used for archiving, research, or statistical work, the required safeguards and conditions must still be followed.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when relying on the Article 14(5)(b) exception for archiving, research, or statistical purposes.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy describe the Article 89 safeguards and conditions applicable when the organization relies on this notice exception?

sub_obligations.legal_text: or in so far as the obligation referred to in paragraph 1 of this Article is likely to render impossible or seriously impair the achievement of the objectives of that processing.
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The exception may also apply when giving the notice would make the purpose of the processing impossible or seriously undermine it.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when providing the Article 14(1) information would likely make the processing purpose impossible or seriously impair its achievement.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy explain when providing the required notice could make the processing purpose impossible or seriously undermine it?

sub_obligations.legal_text: In such cases the controller shall take appropriate measures to protect the data subject’s rights and freedoms and legitimate interests
sub_obligations.plain_summary: When relying on this exception, the organization must use appropriate measures to protect the person's rights, freedoms, and legitimate interests.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when the organization relies on the Article 14(5)(b) exception.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy describe appropriate measures used to protect people's rights, freedoms, and legitimate interests when the normal notice is not provided?

sub_obligations.legal_text: including making the information publicly available;
sub_obligations.plain_summary: Those protective measures may include making the required information publicly available.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when relying on the Article 14(5)(b) exception and public availability is used as a protective measure.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: If the organization relies on public availability as a protective measure, does the policy state that the required information is made publicly available?

sub_obligations.legal_text: obtaining or disclosure is expressly laid down by Union or Member State law to which the controller is subject
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The usual notice requirement may not apply when European or national law expressly requires the information to be obtained or disclosed.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when applicable European or national law expressly requires the information to be obtained or disclosed.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy identify any applicable law that expressly requires the information to be obtained or disclosed and therefore supports this exception?

sub_obligations.legal_text: and which provides appropriate measures to protect the data subject’s legitimate interests;
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The law supporting this exception must include suitable measures protecting the person's legitimate interests.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when relying on the Article 14(5)(c) exception.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy identify the protective measures in the applicable law that safeguard people's legitimate interests?

sub_obligations.legal_text: where the personal data must remain confidential subject to an obligation of professional secrecy regulated by Union or Member State law, including a statutory obligation of secrecy.
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The usual notice requirement may not apply when the information must remain confidential because a professional or legal secrecy obligation applies.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when the personal information is subject to a legally regulated professional or statutory secrecy obligation.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy identify cases where information must remain confidential because a professional or statutory secrecy obligation prevents the usual disclosure?

article_name: Right of access by the data subject

sub_obligations.legal_text: The data subject shall have the right to obtain from the controller confirmation as to whether or not personal data concerning him or her are being processed
sub_obligations.plain_summary: A person can ask the organization to confirm whether it is using personal information about them.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when a person makes an access request.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy state that people can request confirmation of whether the organization is processing personal information about them?

sub_obligations.legal_text: and, where that is the case, access to the personal data
sub_obligations.plain_summary: If the organization is using the person's information, the person can ask to see that information.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when the organization is processing personal information about the person.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy state that people can obtain access to the personal information the organization holds or uses about them?

sub_obligations.legal_text: the purposes of the processing;
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The person can ask why their personal information is being used.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when the person exercises the right of access.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy state that an access response will include the purposes for which the person's personal information is used?

sub_obligations.legal_text: the categories of personal data concerned;
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The person can ask what types of personal information about them are being used.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when the person exercises the right of access.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy state that an access response will identify the types or categories of personal information being processed?

sub_obligations.legal_text: the recipients or categories of recipient to whom the personal data have been or will be disclosed, in particular recipients in third countries or international organisations;
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The person can ask who has received or will receive their personal information, including recipients outside the applicable region or international organizations.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when the person exercises the right of access.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy state that an access response will identify recipients or categories of recipients that have received or will receive the person's personal information, including relevant international recipients?

sub_obligations.legal_text: where possible, the envisaged period for which the personal data will be stored, or, if not possible, the criteria used to determine that period;
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The person can ask how long their information is expected to be kept, or how that period is decided when a fixed period cannot be given.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when the person exercises the right of access.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy state that an access response will provide the expected retention period or, when that cannot be stated, the criteria used to determine it?

sub_obligations.legal_text: the existence of the right to request from the controller rectification or erasure of personal data
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The person must be told that they can ask for their personal information to be corrected or deleted.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when the person exercises the right of access.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy state that an access response will inform the person about their rights to request correction or deletion of their personal information?

sub_obligations.legal_text: or restriction of processing of personal data concerning the data subject
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The person must be told that they can ask the organization to limit how their personal information is used.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when the person exercises the right of access.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy state that an access response will inform the person about their right to request a restriction on the use of their personal information?

sub_obligations.legal_text: or to object to such processing;
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The person must be told that they may have a right to object to the use of their personal information.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when the person exercises the right of access.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy state that an access response will inform the person about their right to object to relevant processing?

sub_obligations.legal_text: the right to lodge a complaint with a supervisory authority;
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The person must be told that they can complain to a privacy regulator.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when the person exercises the right of access.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy state that an access response will inform the person about their right to complain to a supervisory authority?

sub_obligations.legal_text: where the personal data are not collected from the data subject, any available information as to their source;
sub_obligations.plain_summary: If the information came from somewhere other than the person, the person can ask where it came from.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when the personal information was not collected directly from the person.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: If the information was obtained from another source, does the policy state that an access response will provide available information about that source?

sub_obligations.legal_text: the existence of automated decision-making, including profiling, referred to in [Article 22](https://gdpr-info.eu/art-22-gdpr/)(1) and (4)
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The person can be told whether covered decisions about them are made automatically, including through profiling.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when Article 22(1) or 22(4) automated decision-making, including profiling, is used.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: If covered automated decision-making or profiling is used, does the policy state that an access response will disclose its existence?

sub_obligations.legal_text: and, at least in those cases, meaningful information about the logic involved
sub_obligations.plain_summary: For covered automated decisions, the person can ask for meaningful information about how the decision-making works.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when Article 22(1) or 22(4) automated decision-making is used.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: If covered automated decision-making is used, does the policy state that an access response will provide meaningful information about the logic involved?

sub_obligations.legal_text: as well as the significance and the envisaged consequences of such processing for the data subject.
sub_obligations.plain_summary: For covered automated decisions, the person can ask what the processing means for them and what effects are expected.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when Article 22(1) or 22(4) automated decision-making is used.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: If covered automated decision-making is used, does the policy state that an access response will explain its significance and expected consequences for the person?

sub_obligations.legal_text: Where personal data are transferred to a third country or to an international organisation, the data subject shall have the right to be informed of the appropriate safeguards pursuant to [Article 46](https://gdpr-info.eu/art-46-gdpr/) relating to the transfer.
sub_obligations.plain_summary: When personal information is transferred internationally, the person can ask what safeguards under Article 46 protect that transfer.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when the person's personal information is transferred to a third country or international organization and the transfer relies on Article 46 safeguards.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: If the person's information is transferred internationally under Article 46, does the policy state that the person can obtain information about the safeguards protecting the transfer?

sub_obligations.legal_text: The controller shall provide a copy of the personal data undergoing processing.
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The organization must provide the person with a copy of their personal information when they make an access request.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when the person exercises the right of access and the organization is processing their personal information.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy state that people can receive a copy of the personal information being processed about them?

sub_obligations.legal_text: For any further copies requested by the data subject, the controller may charge a reasonable fee based on administrative costs.
sub_obligations.plain_summary: For additional copies beyond the first, the organization may charge a reasonable fee based on the cost of providing them.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when the person requests additional copies after the first copy.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy state that fees for additional copies, if charged, are reasonable and based on administrative costs?

sub_obligations.legal_text: Where the data subject makes the request by electronic means, and unless otherwise requested by the data subject, the information shall be provided in a commonly used electronic form.
sub_obligations.plain_summary: When an access request is made electronically, the information should normally be provided in a commonly used electronic format unless the person asks for another format.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when the access request is made electronically.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy state that electronic access requests will normally receive the requested information in a commonly used electronic format unless the person asks for another format?

sub_obligations.legal_text: The right to obtain a copy referred to in paragraph 3 shall not adversely affect the rights and freedoms of others.
sub_obligations.plain_summary: Providing a copy of someone's information must not unfairly harm other people's rights or freedoms.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when providing a copy of personal information could affect the rights or freedoms of other people.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy describe safeguards or review steps to ensure that providing an access copy does not adversely affect other people's rights or freedoms?

article_name: Right to rectification

sub_obligations.legal_text: The data subject shall have the right to obtain from the controller without undue delay the rectification of inaccurate personal data concerning him or her.
sub_obligations.plain_summary: A person can ask the organization to correct inaccurate personal information about them without unnecessary delay.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when the person's personal information is inaccurate.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy provide a way for people to request correction of inaccurate personal information and state that corrections are made without undue delay?

sub_obligations.legal_text: Taking into account the purposes of the processing, the data subject shall have the right to have incomplete personal data completed, including by means of providing a supplementary statement.
sub_obligations.plain_summary: A person can ask the organization to complete missing personal information when it is needed for the purpose for which the information is used, including by adding a statement from the person.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when the person's personal information is incomplete and completing it is relevant to the purposes for which it is used.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy provide a way for people to request completion of incomplete personal information, including by submitting additional information or a supplementary statement?

article_name: Right to erasure (‘right to be forgotten’)

sub_obligations.legal_text: the personal data are no longer necessary in relation to the purposes for which they were collected or otherwise processed;
sub_obligations.plain_summary: A person can ask for their personal information to be deleted when it is no longer needed for the purpose for which it was collected or used.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when the personal information is no longer necessary for its original or relevant processing purpose.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy provide for deletion when personal information is no longer needed for the purpose for which it was collected or used?

sub_obligations.legal_text: the data subject withdraws consent on which the processing is based according to point (a) of [Article 6](https://gdpr-info.eu/art-6-gdpr/)(1), or point (a) of [Article 9](https://gdpr-info.eu/art-9-gdpr/)(2), and where there is no other legal ground for the processing;
sub_obligations.plain_summary: A person can ask for deletion after withdrawing their permission when permission was the reason for using the information and there is no other valid reason to keep using it.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when processing is based on Article 6(1)(a) or Article 9(2)(a), the person withdraws consent, and no other legal basis supports the processing.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy provide for deletion when a person withdraws consent and no other valid legal basis exists for continuing the processing?

sub_obligations.legal_text: the data subject objects to the processing pursuant to [Article 21](https://gdpr-info.eu/art-21-gdpr/)(1) and there are no overriding legitimate grounds for the processing
sub_obligations.plain_summary: A person can ask for deletion after objecting to processing when there is no stronger valid reason for the organization to continue using the information.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when the person objects under Article 21(1) and no overriding legitimate grounds for the processing exist.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy provide for deletion when a person objects under Article 21(1) and there is no overriding legitimate reason to continue processing?

sub_obligations.legal_text: or the data subject objects to the processing pursuant to [Article 21](https://gdpr-info.eu/art-21-gdpr/)(2);
sub_obligations.plain_summary: A person can ask for deletion when they object to processing covered by Article 21(2).
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when the person objects to processing pursuant to Article 21(2).
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy provide for deletion when a person makes an objection covered by Article 21(2)?

sub_obligations.legal_text: the personal data have been unlawfully processed;
sub_obligations.plain_summary: A person can ask for deletion when their personal information has been used unlawfully.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when the personal information has been processed unlawfully.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy provide for deletion when personal information has been processed unlawfully?

sub_obligations.legal_text: the personal data have to be erased for compliance with a legal obligation in Union or Member State law to which the controller is subject;
sub_obligations.plain_summary: A person can ask for deletion when a European or national law requires the organization to erase the information.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when an applicable European or national legal requirement requires the personal information to be erased.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy provide for deletion when an applicable European or national law requires the information to be erased?

sub_obligations.legal_text: the personal data have been collected in relation to the offer of information society services referred to in [Article 8](https://gdpr-info.eu/art-8-gdpr/)(1).
sub_obligations.plain_summary: A person can ask for deletion when their personal information was collected in connection with an online service covered by the children's consent rules.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when the personal information was collected in connection with an information society service referred to in Article 8(1).
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy provide for deletion of personal information collected in connection with an information society service covered by Article 8(1)?

sub_obligations.legal_text: Where the controller has made the personal data public and is obliged pursuant to paragraph 1 to erase the personal data, the controller, taking account of available technology and the cost of implementation, shall take reasonable steps, including technical measures, to inform controllers which are processing the personal data that the data subject has requested the erasure by such controllers of any links to, or copy or replication of, those personal data.
sub_obligations.plain_summary: When the organization has made someone's information public and must delete it, it must take reasonable technical and other steps to tell other organizations processing that information about the person's deletion request, considering available technology and implementation costs.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when the organization has made the personal information public and is required to erase it under paragraph 1.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy describe reasonable steps, including technical measures where appropriate, to notify other organizations processing publicly disclosed information of a person's erasure request?

sub_obligations.legal_text: for exercising the right of freedom of expression and information;
sub_obligations.plain_summary: Deletion does not have to be carried out when keeping the information is necessary to protect freedom of expression or access to information.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when continued processing is necessary to exercise freedom of expression or information.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy identify freedom of expression or information as a circumstance that may prevent deletion when continued processing is necessary for that purpose?

sub_obligations.legal_text: for compliance with a legal obligation which requires processing by Union or Member State law to which the controller is subject
sub_obligations.plain_summary: Deletion does not have to be carried out when a European or national law requires the organization to keep using the information.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when applicable European or national law requires the processing to continue.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy identify legal requirements that may require continued processing despite an erasure request?

sub_obligations.legal_text: or for the performance of a task carried out in the public interest or in the exercise of official authority vested in the controller;
sub_obligations.plain_summary: Deletion does not have to be carried out when keeping the information is necessary for a public-interest task or official authority given to the organization.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when continued processing is necessary for a public-interest task or the exercise of official authority.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy identify public-interest tasks or official authority as circumstances that may prevent deletion when continued processing is necessary?

sub_obligations.legal_text: for reasons of public interest in the area of public health in accordance with points (h) and (i) of [Article 9](https://gdpr-info.eu/art-9-gdpr/)(2) as well as [Article 9](https://gdpr-info.eu/art-9-gdpr/)(3);
sub_obligations.plain_summary: Deletion does not have to be carried out when keeping the information is necessary for certain public-health purposes allowed under the GDPR.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when continued processing is necessary for a public-health purpose covered by Article 9(2)(h), 9(2)(i), or Article 9(3).
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy identify applicable public-health purposes under Article 9 that may prevent deletion when continued processing is necessary?

sub_obligations.legal_text: for archiving purposes in the public interest, scientific or historical research purposes or statistical purposes in accordance with [Article 89](https://gdpr-info.eu/art-89-gdpr/)(1) in so far as the right referred to in paragraph 1 is likely to render impossible or seriously impair the achievement of the objectives of that processing; or
sub_obligations.plain_summary: Deletion does not have to be carried out when the information is needed for qualifying archiving, research, or statistical work and deletion would make that work impossible or seriously undermine its purpose.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when processing is for public-interest archiving, scientific or historical research, or statistical purposes under Article 89(1), and deletion would likely make the purpose impossible or seriously impair it.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy identify qualifying archiving, research, or statistical purposes for which deletion may be refused because it would make the purpose impossible or seriously undermine it?

sub_obligations.legal_text: for the establishment, exercise or defence of legal claims.
sub_obligations.plain_summary: Deletion does not have to be carried out when keeping the information is necessary to bring, pursue, or defend a legal claim.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when continued processing is necessary to establish, exercise, or defend legal claims.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy identify legal claims as a circumstance that may prevent deletion when retaining the information is necessary for them?

article_name: Right to restriction of processing

sub_obligations.legal_text: the accuracy of the personal data is contested by the data subject, for a period enabling the controller to verify the accuracy of the personal data;
sub_obligations.plain_summary: A person can ask the organization to temporarily limit use of their information while the organization checks whether the information is accurate.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when the person disputes the accuracy of their personal information.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy provide for temporarily restricting use of personal information while a disputed accuracy issue is being verified?

sub_obligations.legal_text: the processing is unlawful and the data subject opposes the erasure of the personal data and requests the restriction of their use instead;
sub_obligations.plain_summary: When information is being used unlawfully, a person can ask the organization to stop using it without deleting it instead.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when the processing is unlawful and the person opposes deletion and requests restricted use instead.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy allow a person to request restricted use instead of deletion when the processing is unlawful?

sub_obligations.legal_text: the controller no longer needs the personal data for the purposes of the processing, but they are required by the data subject for the establishment, exercise or defence of legal claims;
sub_obligations.plain_summary: A person can ask the organization to keep their information but stop using it when the organization no longer needs it but the person needs it for a legal claim.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when the organization no longer needs the information for its processing purpose but the person needs it to establish, pursue, or defend a legal claim.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy provide for restricted use when the organization no longer needs the information but the person needs it for establishing, pursuing, or defending a legal claim?

sub_obligations.legal_text: the data subject has objected to processing pursuant to [Article 21](https://gdpr-info.eu/art-21-gdpr/)(1) pending the verification whether the legitimate grounds of the controller override those of the data subject.
sub_obligations.plain_summary: A person can ask to temporarily limit use of their information after objecting to processing while the organization checks whose interests should prevail.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when the person has objected under Article 21(1) and the organization is still determining whether its grounds override the person's interests.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy provide for temporary restriction of processing while an Article 21(1) objection is being assessed?

sub_obligations.legal_text: Where processing has been restricted under paragraph 1, such personal data shall, with the exception of storage, only be processed with the data subject’s consent
sub_obligations.plain_summary: Once use of information has been restricted, it may generally only be used with the person's permission, apart from simply storing it.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when processing has been restricted under Article 18(1).
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy state that restricted information may only be used with the person's consent, except for storage, unless another permitted exception applies?

sub_obligations.legal_text: or for the establishment, exercise or defence of legal claims
sub_obligations.plain_summary: Restricted information may still be used when necessary to establish, pursue, or defend a legal claim.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when processing has been restricted under Article 18(1) and the information is needed for a legal claim.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy allow restricted information to be used when necessary to establish, pursue, or defend a legal claim?

sub_obligations.legal_text: or for the protection of the rights of another natural or legal person
sub_obligations.plain_summary: Restricted information may still be used when necessary to protect another person's or organization's rights.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when processing has been restricted under Article 18(1) and the processing is necessary to protect another person's or organization's rights.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy allow restricted information to be used when necessary to protect another person's or organization's rights?

sub_obligations.legal_text: or for reasons of important public interest of the Union or of a Member State.
sub_obligations.plain_summary: Restricted information may still be used when necessary for an important public-interest reason recognized by European or national law.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when processing has been restricted under Article 18(1) and the processing is necessary for an important public-interest reason of the European Union or a Member State.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy allow restricted information to be used when necessary for an important public-interest reason of the European Union or a Member State?

sub_obligations.legal_text: A data subject who has obtained restriction of processing pursuant to paragraph 1 shall be informed by the controller before the restriction of processing is lifted.
sub_obligations.plain_summary: A person whose information has been restricted must be told before the organization starts using it normally again.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when a restriction of processing has been granted under Article 18(1).
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy state that a person will be informed before a restriction on processing their information is lifted?

article_name: Notification obligation regarding rectification or erasure of personal data or restriction of processing

sub_obligations.legal_text: The controller shall communicate any rectification or erasure of personal data or restriction of processing carried out in accordance with [Article 16](https://gdpr-info.eu/art-16-gdpr/), [Article 17](https://gdpr-info.eu/art-17-gdpr/)(1) and [Article 18](https://gdpr-info.eu/art-18-gdpr/) to each recipient to whom the personal data have been disclosed
sub_obligations.plain_summary: When personal information is corrected, deleted, or restricted, the organization must tell every recipient that received that information about the change.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when personal information has been corrected, deleted, or restricted under Articles 16, 17(1), or 18 and has previously been disclosed to recipients.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy describe a process for notifying every recipient that received the information when it is corrected, deleted, or restricted?

sub_obligations.legal_text: unless this proves impossible or involves disproportionate effort.
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The organization does not have to notify recipients when doing so is impossible or would require disproportionate effort.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when notifying a recipient is impossible or would involve disproportionate effort.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy define when recipient notification may be skipped because it is impossible or would require disproportionate effort?

sub_obligations.legal_text: The controller shall inform the data subject about those recipients if the data subject requests it.
sub_obligations.plain_summary: If a person asks, the organization must tell them which recipients were notified about the correction, deletion, or restriction.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when the person requests information about the recipients notified.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy provide a process for telling a person which recipients were notified when the person asks for that information?

article_name: Right to data portability

sub_obligations.legal_text: The data subject shall have the right to receive the personal data concerning him or her, which he or she has provided to a controller, in a structured, commonly used and machine-readable format
sub_obligations.plain_summary: A person can ask for the personal information they provided to the organization in a structured, commonly used format that a computer can read.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when the person has provided the personal information to the organization and the conditions in Article 20(1) apply.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy provide a way for eligible people to receive the personal information they provided in a structured, commonly used, machine-readable format?

sub_obligations.legal_text: and have the right to transmit those data to another controller without hindrance from the controller to which the personal data have been provided
sub_obligations.plain_summary: A person can move the personal information they provided to another organization without the original organization creating unnecessary obstacles.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when the conditions in Article 20(1) apply.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy state that eligible people can move the personal information they provided to another organization without unnecessary obstacles from the original organization?

sub_obligations.legal_text: where:
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The portability right applies only when the following legal conditions are met.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when determining whether the right to data portability applies.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy identify the conditions under which the organization provides data portability?

sub_obligations.legal_text: the processing is based on consent pursuant to point (a) of [Article 6](https://gdpr-info.eu/art-6-gdpr/)(1) or point (a) of [Article 9](https://gdpr-info.eu/art-9-gdpr/)(2) or on a contract pursuant to point (b) of [Article 6](https://gdpr-info.eu/art-6-gdpr/)(1);
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The portability right applies when the information is used based on the person's permission or because it is needed to perform a contract.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when processing is based on Article 6(1)(a), Article 9(2)(a), or Article 6(1)(b).
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy identify consent and contract-based processing as the legal bases under which data portability is available?

sub_obligations.legal_text: the processing is carried out by automated means.
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The portability right applies when the information is processed using automated systems.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when processing is carried out by automated means.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy identify automated processing as a condition for providing data portability?

sub_obligations.legal_text: In exercising his or her right to data portability pursuant to paragraph 1, the data subject shall have the right to have the personal data transmitted directly from one controller to another, where technically feasible.
sub_obligations.plain_summary: If technically possible, a person can ask the organization to send their portable information directly to another organization.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when the person is exercising the data portability right and direct transfer is technically feasible.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy provide for direct transfer of portable personal information from the organization to another organization when technically feasible?

sub_obligations.legal_text: The exercise of the right referred to in paragraph 1 of this Article shall be without prejudice to [Article 17](https://gdpr-info.eu/art-17-gdpr/).
sub_obligations.plain_summary: Using the data portability right does not remove or limit the person's separate right to request deletion.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when the person exercises the data portability right.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy preserve the person's separate right to request deletion when they exercise data portability?

sub_obligations.legal_text: That right shall not apply to processing necessary for the performance of a task carried out in the public interest or in the exercise of official authority vested in the controller.
sub_obligations.plain_summary: Data portability does not apply when the information is being used as necessary for a public-interest task or official authority.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when processing is necessary for a public-interest task or the exercise of official authority.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy identify public-interest or official-authority processing as outside the scope of the data portability right where applicable?

sub_obligations.legal_text: The right referred to in paragraph 1 shall not adversely affect the rights and freedoms of others.
sub_obligations.plain_summary: Providing portable information must not unfairly harm other people's rights or freedoms.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when providing portable information could affect other people's rights or freedoms.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy describe safeguards to ensure that fulfilling a portability request does not adversely affect other people's rights or freedoms?

article_name: Right to object

sub_obligations.legal_text: The data subject shall have the right to object, on grounds relating to his or her particular situation, at any time to processing of personal data concerning him or her which is based on point (e) or (f) of [Article 6(](https://gdpr-info.eu/art-6-gdpr/)1), including profiling based on those provisions.
sub_obligations.plain_summary: A person can object at any time to the use of their personal information when it is based on a public-interest task or legitimate interests, including related profiling, when the objection is based on their particular situation.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when processing is based on Article 6(1)(e) or 6(1)(f), including profiling based on those provisions.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy provide a way for people to object at any time to processing based on public-interest tasks or legitimate interests, including related profiling, based on their particular situation?

sub_obligations.legal_text: The controller shall no longer process the personal data unless the controller demonstrates compelling legitimate grounds for the processing which override the interests, rights and freedoms of the data subject
sub_obligations.plain_summary: After a valid objection, the organization must stop the processing unless it can show a strong enough reason to continue that outweighs the person's interests, rights, and freedoms.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only after an objection under Article 21(1) to processing based on Article 6(1)(e) or (f).
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy state that processing will stop after an applicable objection unless the organization can demonstrate compelling grounds that override the person's interests, rights, and freedoms?

sub_obligations.legal_text: or for the establishment, exercise or defence of legal claims.
sub_obligations.plain_summary: After an objection, the organization may also continue using the information when it is needed to establish, pursue, or defend a legal claim.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only after an objection under Article 21(1), where continued processing is necessary for a legal claim.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy identify legal claims as a circumstance in which processing may continue after an Article 21(1) objection?

sub_obligations.legal_text: Where personal data are processed for direct marketing purposes, the data subject shall have the right to object at any time to processing of personal data concerning him or her for such marketing, which includes profiling to the extent that it is related to such direct marketing.
sub_obligations.plain_summary: A person can object at any time to the use of their personal information for direct marketing, including profiling related to that marketing.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when personal information is processed for direct marketing.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy provide a clear way for people to object at any time to direct marketing and related profiling?

sub_obligations.legal_text: Where the data subject objects to processing for direct marketing purposes, the personal data shall no longer be processed for such purposes.
sub_obligations.plain_summary: Once a person objects to direct marketing, their personal information must no longer be used for that marketing.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when the person objects to processing for direct marketing purposes.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy state that personal information will stop being used for direct marketing after the person objects?

sub_obligations.legal_text: At the latest at the time of the first communication with the data subject, the right referred to in paragraphs 1 and 2 shall be explicitly brought to the attention of the data subject
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The person must be explicitly told about their applicable right to object no later than the first time the organization communicates with them.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when the rights under Article 21(1) or 21(2) apply.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy state that the applicable right to object is explicitly communicated to the person no later than the first communication?

sub_obligations.legal_text: and shall be presented clearly and separately from any other information.
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The right to object must be presented clearly and kept separate from other information.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when the rights under Article 21(1) or 21(2) apply and are being communicated.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy state that the right to object is presented clearly and separately from other information?

sub_obligations.legal_text: In the context of the use of information society services, and notwithstanding [Directive 2002/58/EC](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:32002L0058), the data subject may exercise his or her right to object by automated means using technical specifications.
sub_obligations.plain_summary: When using an online service, a person may be able to exercise their objection automatically using suitable technical tools, subject to the applicable ePrivacy rules.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only in the context of information society services.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: For applicable online services, does the policy provide a technical mechanism that allows people to exercise their right to object automatically?

sub_obligations.legal_text: Where personal data are processed for scientific or historical research purposes or statistical purposes pursuant to [Article 89(](https://gdpr-info.eu/art-89-gdpr/)1), the data subject, on grounds relating to his or her particular situation, shall have the right to object to processing of personal data concerning him or her, unless the processing is necessary for the performance of a task carried out for reasons of public interest.
sub_obligations.plain_summary: A person can object to their information being used for qualifying research or statistical purposes based on their particular situation, unless the use is necessary for a public-interest task.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when personal information is processed for scientific research, historical research, or statistical purposes under Article 89(1).
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy provide a way for people to object to qualifying research or statistical processing based on their particular situation, while recognizing the public-interest exception?

article_name: Automated individual decision-making, including profiling

sub_obligations.legal_text: The data subject shall have the right not to be subject to a decision based solely on automated processing, including profiling, which produces legal effects concerning him or her or similarly significantly affects him or her.
sub_obligations.plain_summary: A person has the right not to be subjected to a decision made entirely by automated processing, including profiling, when that decision has legal or similarly significant effects on them.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when a decision is based solely on automated processing, including profiling, and produces legal or similarly significant effects on the person.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy state that people will not be subjected to solely automated decisions, including profiling, that produce legal or similarly significant effects, except where a permitted Article 22(2) exception applies?

sub_obligations.legal_text: is necessary for entering into, or performance of, a contract between the data subject and a data controller;
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The restriction on solely automated decisions does not apply when the automated decision is necessary to enter into or perform a contract with the person.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when the solely automated decision is necessary for entering into or performing a contract with the person.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: If the organization relies on a contract-related exception for a solely automated decision, does the policy state that the decision is necessary to enter into or perform the contract?

sub_obligations.legal_text: is authorised by Union or Member State law to which the controller is subject and which also lays down suitable measures to safeguard the data subject’s rights and freedoms and legitimate interests; or
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The restriction does not apply when European or national law specifically allows the automated decision and that law provides suitable protections for the person's rights and interests.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when applicable European or national law authorizes the solely automated decision and provides suitable safeguards.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: If the organization relies on a legal authorization for a solely automated decision, does the policy identify the applicable law and the safeguards it provides for people's rights and interests?

sub_obligations.legal_text: is based on the data subject’s explicit consent.
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The restriction does not apply when the person has explicitly agreed to the automated decision.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when the solely automated decision is based on the person's explicit consent.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: If the organization relies on explicit consent for a solely automated decision, does the policy state that the decision is based on the person's explicit consent?

sub_obligations.legal_text: In the cases referred to in points (a) and (c) of paragraph 2, the data controller shall implement suitable measures to safeguard the data subject’s rights and freedoms and legitimate interests
sub_obligations.plain_summary: When relying on the contract or explicit-consent exceptions, the organization must put protections in place for the person's rights, freedoms, and interests.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when the solely automated decision relies on the contract exception in Article 22(2)(a) or the explicit-consent exception in Article 22(2)(c).
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Where the contract or explicit-consent exception is used, does the policy describe suitable measures protecting people's rights, freedoms, and legitimate interests?

sub_obligations.legal_text: at least the right to obtain human intervention on the part of the controller
sub_obligations.plain_summary: At a minimum, the person must be able to ask for a human to review or intervene in the automated decision.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when the contract or explicit-consent exception under Article 22(2)(a) or (c) is relied upon.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy give people a right to obtain human intervention in a covered automated decision?

sub_obligations.legal_text: to express his or her point of view
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The person must be able to explain their side or provide their view about the automated decision.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when the contract or explicit-consent exception under Article 22(2)(a) or (c) is relied upon.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy give people an opportunity to express their views about a covered automated decision?

sub_obligations.legal_text: and to contest the decision.
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The person must be able to challenge a covered automated decision.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when the contract or explicit-consent exception under Article 22(2)(a) or (c) is relied upon.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy give people a way to challenge or contest a covered automated decision?

sub_obligations.legal_text: Decisions referred to in paragraph 2 shall not be based on special categories of personal data referred to in [Article 9](https://gdpr-info.eu/art-9-gdpr/)(1)
sub_obligations.plain_summary: A covered automated decision generally cannot use sensitive types of personal information as its basis.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when a decision falls within Article 22(2) and involves special-category personal information under Article 9(1).
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy state that covered automated decisions are not based on special-category personal information unless the Article 22(4) exception applies?

sub_obligations.legal_text: unless point (a) or (g) of [Article 9](https://gdpr-info.eu/art-9-gdpr/)(2) applies
sub_obligations.plain_summary: Sensitive information may be used for a covered automated decision only when one of the specified exceptions for sensitive information applies.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when special-category personal information is used in a covered automated decision.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: If special-category personal information is used in a covered automated decision, does the policy identify an applicable Article 9(2)(a) or 9(2)(g) exception?

sub_obligations.legal_text: and suitable measures to safeguard the data subject’s rights and freedoms and legitimate interests are in place.
sub_obligations.plain_summary: When sensitive information is used under the permitted exception, suitable protections for the person's rights, freedoms, and interests must be in place.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when special-category personal information is used in a covered automated decision under an Article 9(2)(a) or 9(2)(g) exception.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Where special-category personal information is used in a permitted covered automated decision, does the policy describe suitable safeguards protecting the person's rights, freedoms, and legitimate interests?

article_name: Responsibility of the controller

sub_obligations.legal_text: Taking into account the nature, scope, context and purposes of processing as well as the risks of varying likelihood and severity for the rights and freedoms of natural persons, the controller shall implement appropriate technical and organisational measures to ensure and to be able to demonstrate that processing is performed in accordance with this Regulation.
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The organization must put suitable technical and organizational safeguards in place, based on what it does and the risks involved, so that its use of personal information follows the GDPR and it can show that it does so.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy describe risk-based technical and organizational safeguards that the organization uses to comply with GDPR and demonstrate that its processing follows those requirements?

sub_obligations.legal_text: Those measures shall be reviewed and updated where necessary.
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The organization's privacy and security safeguards must be reviewed and updated when needed.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy describe a process for reviewing and updating privacy and security safeguards when necessary?

sub_obligations.legal_text: Where proportionate in relation to processing activities, the measures referred to in paragraph 1 shall include the implementation of appropriate data protection policies by the controller.
sub_obligations.plain_summary: Where appropriate for the organization's processing activities, its safeguards must include suitable privacy policies.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only where implementing data protection policies is proportionate to the organization's processing activities.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Where proportionate to the organization's processing activities, does the policy framework include appropriate data protection policies?

sub_obligations.legal_text: Adherence to approved codes of conduct as referred to in [Article 40](https://gdpr-info.eu/art-40-gdpr/) or approved certification mechanisms as referred to in [Article 42](https://gdpr-info.eu/art-42-gdpr/) may be used as an element by which to demonstrate compliance with the obligations of the controller.
sub_obligations.plain_summary: Following an approved privacy code or certification can be used as evidence that the organization complies with its GDPR responsibilities.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only where the organization chooses to rely on an approved code of conduct or approved certification as evidence of compliance.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: If the organization relies on an approved code of conduct or certification to demonstrate compliance, does the policy identify the relevant code or certification and explain how it supports compliance?

article_name: Data protection by design and by default

sub_obligations.legal_text: Taking into account the state of the art, the cost of implementation and the nature, scope, context and purposes of processing as well as the risks of varying likelihood and severity for rights and freedoms of natural persons posed by the processing, the controller shall, both at the time of the determination of the means for processing and at the time of the processing itself, implement appropriate technical and organisational measures, such as pseudonymisation, which are designed to implement data-protection principles, such as data minimisation, in an effective manner and to integrate the necessary safeguards into the processing in order to meet the requirements of this Regulation and protect the rights of data subjects.
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The organization must build suitable privacy safeguards into its systems and processing from the design stage onward, taking account of available technology, cost, the nature of the processing, and the risks to people, including measures such as pseudonymisation and data minimisation.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy describe a process for building appropriate privacy safeguards into processing when systems and processing methods are designed and when processing takes place, taking account of technology, cost, processing circumstances, and risks?

sub_obligations.legal_text: The controller shall implement appropriate technical and organisational measures for ensuring that, by default, only personal data which are necessary for each specific purpose of the processing are processed.
sub_obligations.plain_summary: By default, the organization should use only the personal information actually needed for each specific purpose.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy describe default settings or controls that limit the collection and use of personal information to what is necessary for each specific purpose?

sub_obligations.legal_text: That obligation applies to the amount of personal data collected
sub_obligations.plain_summary: Default settings must limit how much personal information is collected to what is necessary.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy describe controls that limit the amount of personal information collected by default to what is necessary?

sub_obligations.legal_text: the extent of their processing
sub_obligations.plain_summary: Default settings must limit how extensively personal information is used to what is necessary.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy describe controls that limit the extent of processing by default to what is necessary for the relevant purpose?

sub_obligations.legal_text: the period of their storage
sub_obligations.plain_summary: Default settings must limit how long personal information is stored to what is necessary.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy describe default retention controls that limit storage of personal information to the necessary period?

sub_obligations.legal_text: and their accessibility.
sub_obligations.plain_summary: By default, access to personal information must be limited to what is necessary.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy describe default access controls that limit who can access personal information to what is necessary?

sub_obligations.legal_text: In particular, such measures shall ensure that by default personal data are not made accessible without the individual’s intervention to an indefinite number of natural persons.
sub_obligations.plain_summary: By default, personal information must not be openly accessible to an unlimited number of people without the person's active involvement.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy describe controls that prevent personal information from being automatically accessible to an unlimited number of people without the individual's intervention?

sub_obligations.legal_text: An approved certification mechanism pursuant to [Article 42](https://gdpr-info.eu/art-42-gdpr/) may be used as an element to demonstrate compliance with the requirements set out in paragraphs 1 and 2 of this Article.
sub_obligations.plain_summary: An approved privacy certification can be used as evidence that the organization follows privacy-by-design and privacy-by-default requirements.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only where the organization chooses to use an approved Article 42 certification as evidence of compliance.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: If the organization relies on an approved Article 42 certification to demonstrate compliance, does the policy identify the certification and explain how it supports compliance with privacy-by-design and privacy-by-default requirements?

article_name: Joint controllers

sub_obligations.legal_text: Where two or more controllers jointly determine the purposes and means of processing, they shall be joint controllers.
sub_obligations.plain_summary: When two or more organizations jointly decide why and how personal information is used, they are treated as jointly responsible for that processing.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when two or more organizations jointly determine the purposes and means of processing.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: If the organization jointly decides with another organization why and how personal information is processed, does the policy identify the parties and describe the joint-controller arrangement?

sub_obligations.legal_text: They shall in a transparent manner determine their respective responsibilities for compliance with the obligations under this Regulation
sub_obligations.plain_summary: Jointly responsible organizations must clearly agree who is responsible for which GDPR duties.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when two or more organizations are joint controllers.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy or documented arrangement clearly allocate GDPR responsibilities between the joint controllers?

sub_obligations.legal_text: in particular as regards the exercising of the rights of the data subject
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The arrangement must clearly assign responsibility for handling people's privacy-rights requests.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when two or more organizations are joint controllers.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy or joint-controller arrangement clearly state which organization is responsible for handling people's privacy-rights requests?

sub_obligations.legal_text: and their respective duties to provide the information referred to in [Articles 13](https://gdpr-info.eu/art-13-gdpr/) and [14](https://gdpr-info.eu/art-14-gdpr/),
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The arrangement must clearly assign responsibility for providing the privacy information required when information is collected directly or indirectly.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when two or more organizations are joint controllers.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy or joint-controller arrangement clearly assign responsibility for providing the information required under Articles 13 and 14?

sub_obligations.legal_text: by means of an arrangement between them unless, and in so far as, the respective responsibilities of the controllers are determined by Union or Member State law to which the controllers are subject.
sub_obligations.plain_summary: These responsibilities must normally be set out in an agreement between the organizations unless applicable European or national law already determines who is responsible for them.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when two or more organizations are joint controllers; the agreement requirement does not apply to the extent applicable law already determines the responsibilities.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy or documented arrangement show how the joint controllers' responsibilities are formally determined, either by their agreement or by applicable law?

sub_obligations.legal_text: The arrangement may designate a contact point for data subjects.
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The joint-controller arrangement can name a contact point for people whose information is being processed.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when an organization chooses to designate a contact point for people.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: If the joint-controller arrangement designates a contact point, does the policy identify that contact point and its role?

sub_obligations.legal_text: The arrangement referred to in paragraph 1 shall duly reflect the respective roles and relationships of the joint controllers vis-à-vis the data subjects.
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The joint-controller agreement must accurately explain each organization's role and relationship with the people whose information is processed.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when two or more organizations are joint controllers and have an arrangement under paragraph 1.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the documented joint-controller arrangement accurately describe each organization's role and relationship with the people whose information is processed?

sub_obligations.legal_text: The essence of the arrangement shall be made available to the data subject.
sub_obligations.plain_summary: People must be able to access the main points of the joint-controller agreement.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when two or more organizations are joint controllers and have an arrangement under paragraph 1.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy make the main points of the joint-controller arrangement available to the people whose information is processed?

sub_obligations.legal_text: Irrespective of the terms of the arrangement referred to in paragraph 1, the data subject may exercise his or her rights under this Regulation in respect of and against each of the controllers.
sub_obligations.plain_summary: A person can exercise their GDPR rights against any of the jointly responsible organizations, regardless of how their internal agreement divides responsibilities.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when two or more organizations are joint controllers.
