sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy state that people can exercise their GDPR rights against each joint controller regardless of the internal allocation of responsibilities?

article_name: Processor

sub_obligations.legal_text: Where processing is to be carried out on behalf of a controller, the controller shall use only processors providing sufficient guarantees to implement appropriate technical and organisational measures in such a manner that processing will meet the requirements of this Regulation and ensure the protection of the rights of the data subject.
sub_obligations.plain_summary: When another organization processes personal information on the organization's behalf, the organization must choose providers that can demonstrate suitable privacy and security safeguards.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when another organization processes personal information on behalf of the organization.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy describe a process for selecting processors based on their ability to provide appropriate privacy and security safeguards and protect people's rights?

sub_obligations.legal_text: The processor shall not engage another processor without prior specific or general written authorisation of the controller.
sub_obligations.plain_summary: A service provider cannot appoint another provider to process the information unless the organization has given prior written permission.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when a processor intends to appoint another processor.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy or processor contract require prior written authorization before a processor can appoint another processor?

sub_obligations.legal_text: In the case of general written authorisation, the processor shall inform the controller of any intended changes concerning the addition or replacement of other processors, thereby giving the controller the opportunity to object to such changes.
sub_obligations.plain_summary: If the organization has given general permission for subcontractors, the processor must tell it about planned additions or replacements so it has a chance to object.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when the organization has given general written authorization for subprocessors.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy or processor contract require processors to notify the organization about planned additions or replacements of subprocessors and provide an opportunity to object?

sub_obligations.legal_text: Processing by a processor shall be governed by a contract or other legal act under Union or Member State law, that is binding on the processor with regard to the controller
sub_obligations.plain_summary: Processing by a service provider must be governed by a legally binding agreement or other legal arrangement with the organization.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when a processor is used.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy describe a requirement for every processor relationship to be governed by a binding written contract or other legally valid arrangement?

sub_obligations.legal_text: and that sets out the subject-matter and duration of the processing
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The processor agreement must state what processing is covered and how long it will continue.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when a processor is used and a processor agreement is required.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy or processor agreement specify what processing activities are covered and their duration?

sub_obligations.legal_text: the nature and purpose of the processing
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The processor agreement must explain how and why the information will be processed.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when a processor is used and a processor agreement is required.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy or processor agreement specify the nature and purposes of the processing?

sub_obligations.legal_text: the type of personal data and categories of data subjects
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The processor agreement must identify the types of personal information involved and the groups of people it relates to.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when a processor is used and a processor agreement is required.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy or processor agreement identify the types of personal information processed and the categories of people concerned?

sub_obligations.legal_text: and the obligations and rights of the controller.
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The processor agreement must describe the organization's rights and responsibilities.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when a processor is used and a processor agreement is required.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy or processor agreement clearly set out the organization's rights and obligations?

sub_obligations.legal_text: processes the personal data only on documented instructions from the controller, including with regard to transfers of personal data to a third country or an international organisation, unless required to do so by Union or Member State law to which the processor is subject;
sub_obligations.plain_summary: A processor must use personal information only according to the organization's documented instructions, including instructions about international transfers, unless a law requires the processor to do otherwise.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when a processor processes personal information on the organization's behalf.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy or processor agreement require processors to process personal information only according to documented instructions, including instructions concerning international transfers?

sub_obligations.legal_text: in such a case, the processor shall inform the controller of that legal requirement before processing, unless that law prohibits such information on important grounds of public interest;
sub_obligations.plain_summary: If a law requires the processor to process information contrary to the organization's instructions, the processor must normally tell the organization before doing so.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when a law requires the processor to process personal information contrary to the organization's instructions.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy or processor agreement require a processor to notify the organization before processing required by law, unless the law prohibits that notification?

sub_obligations.legal_text: ensures that persons authorised to process the personal data have committed themselves to confidentiality or are under an appropriate statutory obligation of confidentiality;
sub_obligations.plain_summary: People allowed to handle the information must be bound by confidentiality duties.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when persons are authorized to process personal information.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy or processor agreement require authorized personnel who handle personal information to be bound by confidentiality obligations?

sub_obligations.legal_text: takes all measures required pursuant to [Article 32](https://gdpr-info.eu/art-32-gdpr/);
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The processor must implement the security measures required by Article 32.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when a processor is used.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy or processor agreement require processors to implement the security measures required by Article 32?

sub_obligations.legal_text: respects the conditions referred to in paragraphs 2 and 4 for engaging another processor;
sub_obligations.plain_summary: A processor must follow the required rules when appointing another processor.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when a processor engages another processor.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy or processor agreement require processors to comply with the authorization and contractual requirements for appointing subprocessors?

sub_obligations.legal_text: taking into account the nature of the processing, assists the controller by appropriate technical and organisational measures, insofar as this is possible, for the fulfilment of the controller’s obligation to respond to requests for exercising the data subject’s rights laid down in [Chapter III;](https://gdpr-info.eu/chapter-3/)
sub_obligations.plain_summary: A processor must help the organization handle people's privacy-rights requests using suitable technical and organizational measures where possible.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when a processor is used and assistance with people's privacy-rights requests is relevant and possible given the nature of the processing.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy or processor agreement require processors to assist the organization with responding to people's privacy-rights requests?

sub_obligations.legal_text: assists the controller in ensuring compliance with the obligations pursuant to [Articles 32](https://gdpr-info.eu/art-32-gdpr/) to [36](https://gdpr-info.eu/art-36-gdpr/) taking into account the nature of processing and the information available to the processor;
sub_obligations.plain_summary: A processor must help the organization meet its security, breach, impact-assessment, and regulator-consultation responsibilities to the extent relevant and possible.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when a processor is used and assistance under Articles 32 to 36 is relevant to the processing.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy or processor agreement require processors to assist the organization with its obligations under Articles 32 to 36?

sub_obligations.legal_text: at the choice of the controller, deletes or returns all the personal data to the controller after the end of the provision of services relating to processing,
sub_obligations.plain_summary: When the service ends, the processor must, according to the organization's choice, either return all personal information or delete it.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when the processor's services involving personal information have ended.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy or processor agreement specify that, when processing services end, the organization can require the processor to return or delete all personal information?

sub_obligations.legal_text: and deletes existing copies unless Union or Member State law requires storage of the personal data;
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The processor must delete its remaining copies unless European or national law requires it to keep them.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when the processor's services involving personal information have ended and copies remain.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy or processor agreement require processors to delete remaining copies after the service ends unless applicable law requires retention?

sub_obligations.legal_text: makes available to the controller all information necessary to demonstrate compliance with the obligations laid down in this Article
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The processor must provide the organization with the information it needs to show that the processor is meeting its GDPR responsibilities.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when the organization needs information from the processor to demonstrate compliance.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy or processor agreement require processors to provide information needed to demonstrate their compliance with Article 28?

sub_obligations.legal_text: and allow for and contribute to audits, including inspections, conducted by the controller or another auditor mandated by the controller.
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The processor must allow and support audits or inspections carried out by the organization or its appointed auditor.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when an audit or inspection of the processor is conducted or required.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy or processor agreement give the organization or its appointed auditor audit and inspection rights over the processor?

sub_obligations.legal_text: With regard to point (h) of the first subparagraph, the processor shall immediately inform the controller if, in its opinion, an instruction infringes this Regulation or other Union or Member State data protection provisions.
sub_obligations.plain_summary: A processor must immediately warn the organization if it believes an instruction violates GDPR or other applicable privacy law.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when a processor believes that an instruction from the organization violates applicable data-protection law.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy or processor agreement require processors to immediately notify the organization if they believe an instruction violates GDPR or other applicable data-protection law?

sub_obligations.legal_text: Where a processor engages another processor for carrying out specific processing activities on behalf of the controller, the same data protection obligations as set out in the contract or other legal act between the controller and the processor as referred to in paragraph 3 shall be imposed on that other processor by way of a contract or other legal act under Union or Member State law
sub_obligations.plain_summary: When a processor appoints a subcontractor, the subcontractor must be bound by the same relevant privacy obligations through a legally binding agreement.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when a processor appoints another processor to carry out processing activities.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy or processor agreement require every subprocessor to be bound by the same applicable data-protection obligations through a binding contract or legal arrangement?

sub_obligations.legal_text: in particular providing sufficient guarantees to implement appropriate technical and organisational measures in such a manner that the processing will meet the requirements of this Regulation.
sub_obligations.plain_summary: A subcontractor must provide sufficient guarantees that it can maintain suitable technical and organizational safeguards and process information in accordance with GDPR.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when a processor appoints another processor.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy or processor agreement require subprocessors to provide sufficient guarantees of appropriate privacy and security safeguards and GDPR-compliant processing?

sub_obligations.legal_text: Where that other processor fails to fulfil its data protection obligations, the initial processor shall remain fully liable to the controller for the performance of that other processor’s obligations.
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The original processor remains fully responsible to the organization if its subcontractor fails to meet the required privacy obligations.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when a processor has appointed another processor and that subcontractor fails to meet its data-protection obligations.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy or processor agreement state that the original processor remains fully responsible to the organization for a subprocessor's data-protection obligations?

sub_obligations.legal_text: Adherence of a processor to an approved code of conduct as referred to in [Article 40](https://gdpr-info.eu/art-40-gdpr/) or an approved certification mechanism as referred to in [Article 42](https://gdpr-info.eu/art-42-gdpr/) may be used as an element by which to demonstrate sufficient guarantees as referred to in paragraphs 1 and 4 of this Article.
sub_obligations.plain_summary: A processor's approved privacy certification or code of conduct can be used as evidence that it provides suitable privacy and security guarantees.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only where an approved code of conduct or certification is used as evidence of a processor's guarantees.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: If the organization relies on an approved code of conduct or certification to assess a processor's guarantees, does the policy identify how that evidence is considered?

sub_obligations.legal_text: Without prejudice to an individual contract between the controller and the processor, the contract or the other legal act referred to in paragraphs 3 and 4 of this Article may be based, in whole or in part, on standard contractual clauses referred to in paragraphs 7 and 8 of this Article, including when they are part of a certification granted to the controller or processor pursuant to [Articles 42 ](https://gdpr-info.eu/art-42-gdpr/)and [43](https://gdpr-info.eu/art-43-gdpr/).
sub_obligations.plain_summary: A processor agreement may use approved standard contractual clauses, in whole or in part, while still allowing the parties to have their own individual contract.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when the parties choose to base their processor agreement on applicable standard contractual clauses.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: If standard contractual clauses are used for processor arrangements, does the policy identify that they may form part or all of the applicable processor agreement?

sub_obligations.legal_text: The contract or the other legal act referred to in paragraphs 3 and 4 of this Article shall be in writing, including in electronic form.
sub_obligations.plain_summary: Processor and subprocessor agreements must be documented in writing, including electronically.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when a processor or subprocessor arrangement under paragraphs 3 or 4 exists.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy require processor and subprocessor arrangements to be documented in writing, including electronic form?

sub_obligations.legal_text: Without prejudice to [Articles 82](https://gdpr-info.eu/art-82-gdpr/), [83](https://gdpr-info.eu/art-83-gdpr/) and [84](https://gdpr-info.eu/art-84-gdpr/), if a processor infringes this Regulation by determining the purposes and means of processing, the processor shall be considered to be a controller in respect of that processing.
sub_obligations.plain_summary: If a service provider decides why and how personal information is processed instead of following the organization's instructions, it is treated as responsible as a controller for that processing.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when a processor determines the purposes and means of processing and thereby acts contrary to its processor role.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy explain that a processor that independently determines why and how personal information is processed may be treated as a controller for that processing?

article_name: Records of processing activities

sub_obligations.legal_text: Each controller and, where applicable, the controller’s representative, shall maintain a record of processing activities under its responsibility.
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The organization must keep a record of the personal-information processing activities it is responsible for, where this requirement applies.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Does not apply to an enterprise or organization employing fewer than 250 people unless one of the conditions in Article 30(5) applies.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy or compliance documentation describe a maintained record of the organization's processing activities and identify when the Article 30(5) small-organization exception does or does not apply?

sub_obligations.legal_text: the name and contact details of the controller and, where applicable, the joint controller, the controller’s representative and the data protection officer;
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The record must include the names and contact details of the organization and, where relevant, its joint organizations, representative, and privacy officer.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when maintaining a controller record under Article 30(1); joint controller, representative, or privacy officer details apply where those roles exist.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the processing record contain the required names and contact details for the organization and, where applicable, joint controllers, its representative, and its privacy officer?

sub_obligations.legal_text: the purposes of the processing;
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The record must state why each processing activity is carried out.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when maintaining a controller record under Article 30(1).
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the processing record document the purposes for which personal information is processed?

sub_obligations.legal_text: a description of the categories of data subjects and of the categories of personal data;
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The record must describe the types of people whose information is processed and the types of personal information involved.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when maintaining a controller record under Article 30(1).
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the processing record describe the categories of people concerned and the categories of personal information processed?

sub_obligations.legal_text: the categories of recipients to whom the personal data have been or will be disclosed including recipients in third countries or international organisations;
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The record must identify the types of organizations or people that receive or will receive the personal information, including recipients outside the EU or international organizations.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when maintaining a controller record under Article 30(1).
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the processing record identify the categories of recipients that receive or will receive personal information, including relevant international recipients?

sub_obligations.legal_text: where applicable, transfers of personal data to a third country or an international organisation, including the identification of that third country or international organisation and, in the case of transfers referred to in the second subparagraph of [Article 49](https://gdpr-info.eu/art-49-gdpr/)(1), the documentation of suitable safeguards;
sub_obligations.plain_summary: When relevant, the record must document international transfers, identify the destination country or organization, and document suitable safeguards for the specified Article 49 transfers.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when personal information is transferred to a third country or international organization.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: If international transfers occur, does the processing record identify the destination and document the required safeguards for transfers covered by the second subparagraph of Article 49(1)?

sub_obligations.legal_text: where possible, the envisaged time limits for erasure of the different categories of data;
sub_obligations.plain_summary: Where possible, the record must state how long different types of personal information are expected to be kept before deletion.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only where envisaged deletion time limits can be specified.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Where possible, does the processing record document the expected deletion time limits for different categories of personal information?

sub_obligations.legal_text: where possible, a general description of the technical and organisational security measures referred to in [Article 32](https://gdpr-info.eu/art-32-gdpr/)(1).
sub_obligations.plain_summary: Where possible, the record must give a general description of the technical and organizational security measures used to protect the information.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only where a general description of the Article 32 security measures can be provided.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Where possible, does the processing record contain a general description of the technical and organizational security measures used to protect personal information?

sub_obligations.legal_text: Each processor and, where applicable, the processor’s representative shall maintain a record of all categories of processing activities carried out on behalf of a controller, containing:
sub_obligations.plain_summary: A service provider processing information for an organization must keep a record of the categories of processing it performs for that organization, where this requirement applies.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when the organization acts as a processor or processor representative; the Article 30(5) small-organization exception may apply.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy or compliance documentation describe a maintained record of processing categories carried out on behalf of each organization and address whether the Article 30(5) exception applies?

sub_obligations.legal_text: the name and contact details of the processor or processors and of each controller on behalf of which the processor is acting, and, where applicable, of the controller’s or the processor’s representative, and the data protection officer;
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The processor's record must include the names and contact details of the processor, each organization it works for, and, where relevant, their representatives and privacy officer.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when maintaining a processor record under Article 30(2); representative and privacy officer details apply where those roles exist.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the processor record contain the required names and contact details for the processor, each organization it acts for, and where applicable their representatives and privacy officer?

sub_obligations.legal_text: the categories of processing carried out on behalf of each controller;
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The processor's record must describe the types of processing it performs for each organization it serves.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when maintaining a processor record under Article 30(2).
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the processor record describe the categories of processing performed on behalf of each organization?

sub_obligations.legal_text: where applicable, transfers of personal data to a third country or an international organisation, including the identification of that third country or international organisation and, in the case of transfers referred to in the second subparagraph of [Article 49](https://gdpr-info.eu/art-49-gdpr/)(1), the documentation of suitable safeguards;
sub_obligations.plain_summary: When relevant, the processor's record must document international transfers, identify the destination country or organization, and document suitable safeguards for the specified Article 49 transfers.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when the processor transfers personal information to a third country or international organization.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: If international transfers occur, does the processor record identify the destination and document the required safeguards for transfers covered by the second subparagraph of Article 49(1)?

sub_obligations.legal_text: where possible, a general description of the technical and organisational security measures referred to in [Article 32](https://gdpr-info.eu/art-32-gdpr/)(1).
sub_obligations.plain_summary: Where possible, the processor's record must give a general description of the technical and organizational security measures used to protect the information.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only where a general description of the Article 32 security measures can be provided.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Where possible, does the processor record contain a general description of the technical and organizational security measures used to protect personal information?

sub_obligations.legal_text: The records referred to in paragraphs 1 and 2 shall be in writing, including in electronic form.
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The required processing records must be kept in written form, including electronically.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when a record is required under Article 30(1) or 30(2).
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy or record-management procedure require Article 30 records to be maintained in written or electronic form?

sub_obligations.legal_text: The controller or the processor and, where applicable, the controller’s or the processor’s representative, shall make the record available to the supervisory authority on request.
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The organization or service provider must be able to provide its processing record to the privacy regulator when requested.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when a supervisory authority requests the processing record.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy describe a process for making the relevant processing record available to a supervisory authority when requested?

sub_obligations.legal_text: The obligations referred to in paragraphs 1 and 2 shall not apply to an enterprise or an organisation employing fewer than 250 persons unless the processing it carries out is likely to result in a risk to the rights and freedoms of data subjects
sub_obligations.plain_summary: Organizations with fewer than 250 employees generally do not have to keep these records unless their processing is likely to create risks to people's rights and freedoms.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only for organizations employing fewer than 250 people.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: If the organization has fewer than 250 employees, does the policy explain whether its processing is likely to create risks to people's rights and freedoms and therefore whether the record-keeping requirement applies?

sub_obligations.legal_text: the processing is not occasional
sub_obligations.plain_summary: Organizations with fewer than 250 employees generally do not receive the exception when their processing is carried out regularly rather than only occasionally.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only for organizations employing fewer than 250 people where processing is not occasional.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: If the organization has fewer than 250 employees, does the policy assess whether its processing is regular rather than occasional?

sub_obligations.legal_text: or the processing includes special categories of data as referred to in [Article 9](https://gdpr-info.eu/art-9-gdpr/)(1) or personal data relating to criminal convictions and offences referred to in [Article 10](https://gdpr-info.eu/art-10-gdpr/).
sub_obligations.plain_summary: Organizations with fewer than 250 employees generally do not receive the exception when they handle sensitive information covered by Article 9 or criminal-conviction and offence information covered by Article 10.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only for organizations employing fewer than 250 people that process Article 9 special-category information or Article 10 criminal-conviction and offence information.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: If the organization has fewer than 250 employees, does the policy assess whether it processes special-category information or criminal-conviction and offence information that removes the small-organization exception?

article_name: Security of processing

sub_obligations.legal_text: Taking into account the state of the art, the costs of implementation and the nature, scope, context and purposes of processing as well as the risk of varying likelihood and severity for the rights and freedoms of natural persons, the controller and the processor shall implement appropriate technical and organisational measures to ensure a level of security appropriate to the risk, including inter alia as appropriate:
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The organization and its service providers must use security measures that are appropriate to the risks, taking account of current technology, implementation costs, and the nature and purpose of the processing.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy describe a risk-based process for selecting and implementing security measures, taking account of current technology, cost, processing circumstances, and risks to people?

sub_obligations.legal_text: the pseudonymisation and encryption of personal data;
sub_obligations.plain_summary: Where appropriate to the risk, the organization must use techniques such as pseudonymisation and encryption to protect personal information.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only where these measures are appropriate to the risks of the processing.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy describe the use of pseudonymisation and encryption as security measures where appropriate to the risks?

sub_obligations.legal_text: the ability to ensure the ongoing confidentiality, integrity, availability and resilience of processing systems and services;
sub_obligations.plain_summary: Security measures must support the continued privacy, accuracy, availability, and resilience of systems and services used to process personal information.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy describe measures that maintain confidentiality, integrity, availability, and resilience of systems and services used to process personal information?

sub_obligations.legal_text: the ability to restore the availability and access to personal data in a timely manner in the event of a physical or technical incident;
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The organization must be able to restore access to personal information within an appropriate timeframe after a physical or technical incident.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when a physical or technical incident affects the availability or access to personal information.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy describe backup, recovery, or other measures that allow timely restoration of access to personal information after a physical or technical incident?

sub_obligations.legal_text: a process for regularly testing, assessing and evaluating the effectiveness of technical and organisational measures for ensuring the security of the processing.
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The organization must regularly test and review whether its technical and organizational security measures actually work.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy describe a process for regularly testing, assessing, and evaluating the effectiveness of security measures?

sub_obligations.legal_text: In assessing the appropriate level of security account shall be taken in particular of the risks that are presented by processing
sub_obligations.plain_summary: When deciding how much security is needed, the organization must consider the risks created by its processing activities.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy describe a process for considering processing-related risks when determining the appropriate level of security?

sub_obligations.legal_text: in particular from accidental or unlawful destruction, loss, alteration, unauthorised disclosure of, or access to personal data transmitted, stored or otherwise processed.
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The security assessment must specifically consider risks such as accidental or unlawful destruction, loss, alteration, unauthorized disclosure, and unauthorized access to personal information.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy's security-risk assessment explicitly consider risks of destruction, loss, alteration, unauthorized disclosure, and unauthorized access to personal information?

sub_obligations.legal_text: Adherence to an approved code of conduct as referred to in [Article 40](https://gdpr-info.eu/art-40-gdpr/) or an approved certification mechanism as referred to in [Article 42](https://gdpr-info.eu/art-42-gdpr/) may be used as an element by which to demonstrate compliance with the requirements set out in paragraph 1 of this Article.
sub_obligations.plain_summary: An approved privacy code or certification can be used as evidence that the organization meets the security requirements.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only where the organization chooses to rely on an approved code of conduct or certification as evidence of security compliance.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: If the organization relies on an approved code of conduct or certification to demonstrate security compliance, does the policy identify the relevant code or certification and explain how it supports compliance?

sub_obligations.legal_text: The controller and processor shall take steps to ensure that any natural person acting under the authority of the controller or the processor who has access to personal data does not process them except on instructions from the controller, unless he or she is required to do so by Union or Member State law.
sub_obligations.plain_summary: People who have access to personal information must only use it according to the organization's instructions unless a law requires them to do otherwise.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when a person acts under the organization's or processor's authority and has access to personal information.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy describe controls ensuring that people with access to personal information process it only according to authorized instructions unless applicable law requires otherwise?

article_name: Notification of a personal data breach to the supervisory authority

sub_obligations.legal_text: In the case of a personal data breach, the controller shall without undue delay and, where feasible, not later than 72 hours after having become aware of it, notify the personal data breach to the supervisory authority competent in accordance with [Article 55](https://gdpr-info.eu/art-55-gdpr/), unless the personal data breach is unlikely to result in a risk to the rights and freedoms of natural persons.
sub_obligations.plain_summary: When a personal information breach occurs and is likely to create a risk to people, the organization must report it to the appropriate privacy regulator without unnecessary delay and, where possible, within 72 hours of discovering it.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when a personal data breach occurs and the breach is not unlikely to result in a risk to people's rights and freedoms.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy describe a process for assessing breaches and notifying the appropriate supervisory authority without undue delay and, where feasible, within 72 hours when the breach is likely to create a risk?

sub_obligations.legal_text: Where the notification to the supervisory authority is not made within 72 hours, it shall be accompanied by reasons for the delay.
sub_obligations.plain_summary: If the regulator is notified more than 72 hours after the breach was discovered, the organization must explain why the notification was late.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when a required breach notification is made more than 72 hours after the organization became aware of the breach.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy require reasons for any delay when a required breach notification is submitted more than 72 hours after the breach was discovered?

sub_obligations.legal_text: The processor shall notify the controller without undue delay after becoming aware of a personal data breach.
sub_obligations.plain_summary: A service provider must promptly tell the organization when it becomes aware of a personal information breach.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when a processor becomes aware of a personal data breach.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy or processor agreement require processors to notify the organization without undue delay after becoming aware of a personal data breach?

sub_obligations.legal_text: describe the nature of the personal data breach including where possible, the categories and approximate number of data subjects concerned and the categories and approximate number of personal data records concerned;
sub_obligations.plain_summary: A breach report must explain what happened and, where possible, estimate the types and number of people and personal-information records affected.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when a breach notification to the supervisory authority is required.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy describe a breach-notification process that records the nature of the breach and, where possible, the affected types and approximate numbers of people and records?

sub_obligations.legal_text: communicate the name and contact details of the data protection officer or other contact point where more information can be obtained;
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The breach report must provide the name and contact details of the privacy officer or another person who can provide more information.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when a breach notification to the supervisory authority is required.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy's breach-notification procedure require the notification to include the name and contact details of the privacy officer or another appropriate contact point?

sub_obligations.legal_text: describe the likely consequences of the personal data breach;
sub_obligations.plain_summary: A breach report must explain the likely effects of the breach on the people or information involved.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when a breach notification to the supervisory authority is required.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy's breach-notification procedure require the likely consequences of the breach to be described?

sub_obligations.legal_text: describe the measures taken or proposed to be taken by the controller to address the personal data breach, including, where appropriate, measures to mitigate its possible adverse effects.
sub_obligations.plain_summary: A breach report must explain what the organization has done or plans to do to address the breach and, where appropriate, reduce its harmful effects.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when a breach notification to the supervisory authority is required.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy's breach-notification procedure require the organization to describe measures already taken or planned to address the breach and reduce possible harm?

sub_obligations.legal_text: Where, and in so far as, it is not possible to provide the information at the same time, the information may be provided in phases without undue further delay.
sub_obligations.plain_summary: If all required breach information is not available at once, the organization may provide it in stages but must provide the missing information without unnecessary further delay.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when all required breach-notification information cannot be provided at the same time.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy describe a process for submitting breach information in stages when necessary and providing additional information without undue further delay?

sub_obligations.legal_text: The controller shall document any personal data breaches, comprising the facts relating to the personal data breach, its effects and the remedial action taken.
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The organization must keep records of every personal information breach, including what happened, its effects, and what was done to fix or contain it.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Whenever a personal data breach occurs.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy describe a process for documenting every personal data breach, including its facts, effects, and remedial actions?

sub_obligations.legal_text: That documentation shall enable the supervisory authority to verify compliance with this Article.
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The breach records must contain enough information for the privacy regulator to check whether the organization followed these breach-notification requirements.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Whenever a personal data breach is documented.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy require breach records to contain enough information for a supervisory authority to verify compliance with Article 33?

article_name: Communication of a personal data breach to the data subject

sub_obligations.legal_text: When the personal data breach is likely to result in a high risk to the rights and freedoms of natural persons, the controller shall communicate the personal data breach to the data subject without undue delay.
sub_obligations.plain_summary: When a personal information breach is likely to seriously affect people, the organization must inform the affected people without unnecessary delay.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when a personal data breach is likely to result in a high risk to people's rights and freedoms.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy describe a process for assessing the risk of a personal data breach and promptly notifying affected people when the breach is likely to create a high risk?

sub_obligations.legal_text: The communication to the data subject referred to in paragraph 1 of this Article shall describe in clear and plain language the nature of the personal data breach
sub_obligations.plain_summary: A breach notice to affected people must clearly and simply explain what happened.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when a high-risk personal data breach requires communication to affected people.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the breach-notification procedure require notices to affected people to explain the nature of the breach in clear and plain language?

sub_obligations.legal_text: and contain at least the information and measures referred to in points (b), (c) and (d) of [Article 33](https://gdpr-info.eu/art-33-gdpr/)(3).
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The notice must also provide a contact for more information, explain the likely consequences, and describe what has been or will be done to address the breach and reduce possible harm.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when a high-risk personal data breach requires communication to affected people.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the breach-notification procedure require notices to include a contact for further information, the likely consequences of the breach, and the measures taken or planned to address it and reduce possible harm?

sub_obligations.legal_text: the controller has implemented appropriate technical and organisational protection measures, and those measures were applied to the personal data affected by the personal data breach, in particular those that render the personal data unintelligible to any person who is not authorised to access it, such as encryption;
sub_obligations.plain_summary: Individual notification is not required when suitable protection measures, such as encryption, were already applied to the affected information and make it unintelligible to unauthorized people.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when deciding whether to notify people after a high-risk personal data breach.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: If the organization does not individually notify affected people, does the policy document a condition under which appropriate protection measures, such as encryption, were already applied to the affected information and made it unintelligible to unauthorized people?

sub_obligations.legal_text: the controller has taken subsequent measures which ensure that the high risk to the rights and freedoms of data subjects referred to in paragraph 1 is no longer likely to materialise;
sub_obligations.plain_summary: Individual notification is not required when later actions have removed the likelihood that the serious harm from the breach will occur.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when deciding whether to notify people after a high-risk personal data breach.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: If the organization does not individually notify affected people, does the policy document a condition under which later measures have made the high risk no longer likely to occur?

sub_obligations.legal_text: it would involve disproportionate effort.
sub_obligations.plain_summary: Individual notification is not required when contacting each affected person would require disproportionate effort.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when individual notification would involve disproportionate effort.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: If the organization does not individually notify affected people, does the policy allow this only where doing so would require disproportionate effort?

sub_obligations.legal_text: In such a case, there shall instead be a public communication or similar measure whereby the data subjects are informed in an equally effective manner.
sub_obligations.plain_summary: When individual notification would require disproportionate effort, the organization must instead use a public notice or another method that informs affected people just as effectively.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when individual notification would involve disproportionate effort and the organization relies on that exception.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy require an equally effective public announcement or similar communication when individual notification is not feasible because it would require disproportionate effort?

sub_obligations.legal_text: If the controller has not already communicated the personal data breach to the data subject, the supervisory authority, having considered the likelihood of the personal data breach resulting in a high risk, may require it to do so
sub_obligations.plain_summary: If the organization has not informed affected people, the privacy regulator can require it to do so after assessing the risk.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when the organization has not already communicated a relevant breach to affected people and the supervisory authority assesses it as presenting a high risk.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy acknowledge that the supervisory authority may require affected people to be notified when the organization has not already done so?

sub_obligations.legal_text: or may decide that any of the conditions referred to in paragraph 3 are met.
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The privacy regulator can also decide that one of the exceptions to individual notification applies.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when the supervisory authority reviews a breach that has not already been communicated to affected people.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy acknowledge that the supervisory authority may determine that an exception to individual breach notification applies?

article_name: Data protection impact assessment

sub_obligations.legal_text: Where a type of processing in particular using new technologies, and taking into account the nature, scope, context and purposes of the processing, is likely to result in a high risk to the rights and freedoms of natural persons, the controller shall, prior to the processing, carry out an assessment of the impact of the envisaged processing operations on the protection of personal data.
sub_obligations.plain_summary: Before starting processing that is likely to create a high risk to people, especially when new technology is involved, the organization must carry out a privacy impact assessment.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when the planned processing is likely to result in a high risk to people's rights and freedoms.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy describe a process for identifying high-risk processing and completing a privacy impact assessment before that processing begins?

sub_obligations.legal_text: A single assessment may address a set of similar processing operations that present similar high risks.
sub_obligations.plain_summary: One privacy impact assessment can cover several similar processing activities when they create similar high risks.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when multiple processing activities are sufficiently similar and present similar high risks.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: If one impact assessment is used for multiple processing activities, does the policy explain that the activities must be similar and present similar high risks?

sub_obligations.legal_text: The controller shall seek the advice of the data protection officer, where designated, when carrying out a data protection impact assessment.
sub_obligations.plain_summary: When a privacy officer has been appointed, the organization must ask for that person's advice when carrying out a privacy impact assessment.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when a data protection officer has been designated and a data protection impact assessment is being carried out.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy require the designated privacy officer to be consulted when a data protection impact assessment is carried out?

sub_obligations.legal_text: a systematic and extensive evaluation of personal aspects relating to natural persons which is based on automated processing, including profiling, and on which decisions are based that produce legal effects concerning the natural person or similarly significantly affect the natural person;
sub_obligations.plain_summary: A privacy impact assessment is required when the organization systematically and extensively evaluates people using automated processing or profiling and uses that evaluation to make decisions that have major effects on them.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when there is systematic and extensive automated evaluation or profiling that leads to legally or similarly significant decisions about people.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy require a privacy impact assessment for systematic and extensive automated evaluation or profiling that is used to make legally or similarly significant decisions about people?

sub_obligations.legal_text: processing on a large scale of special categories of data referred to in [Article 9](https://gdpr-info.eu/art-9-gdpr/)(1), or of personal data relating to criminal convictions and offences referred to in [Article 10](https://gdpr-info.eu/art-10-gdpr/); or
sub_obligations.plain_summary: A privacy impact assessment is required when the organization processes large amounts of sensitive information or information about criminal convictions and offences.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when processing special-category information under Article 9(1), or criminal-conviction and offence information under Article 10, on a large scale.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy require a privacy impact assessment for large-scale processing of sensitive information covered by Article 9 or criminal-conviction and offence information covered by Article 10?

sub_obligations.legal_text: a systematic monitoring of a publicly accessible area on a large scale.
sub_obligations.plain_summary: A privacy impact assessment is required when the organization systematically monitors a publicly accessible area on a large scale.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when the organization systematically monitors a publicly accessible area on a large scale.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy require a privacy impact assessment for systematic large-scale monitoring of publicly accessible areas?

sub_obligations.legal_text: a systematic description of the envisaged processing operations and the purposes of the processing, including, where applicable, the legitimate interest pursued by the controller;
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The privacy impact assessment must clearly describe what processing is planned, why it will be carried out, and, when relevant, the organization's reason for relying on its own interests.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when a data protection impact assessment is required.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the impact assessment document provide a systematic description of the planned processing, its purposes, and, where relevant, the organization's stated interest for carrying it out?

sub_obligations.legal_text: an assessment of the necessity and proportionality of the processing operations in relation to the purposes;
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The privacy impact assessment must examine whether the planned processing is necessary and proportionate for its stated purposes.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when a data protection impact assessment is required.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the impact assessment evaluate whether each planned processing activity is necessary and proportionate for its purpose?

sub_obligations.legal_text: an assessment of the risks to the rights and freedoms of data subjects referred to in paragraph 1; and
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The privacy impact assessment must evaluate the risks that the planned processing creates for people.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when a data protection impact assessment is required.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the impact assessment evaluate the risks that the planned processing creates for people's rights and freedoms?

sub_obligations.legal_text: the measures envisaged to address the risks, including safeguards, security measures and mechanisms to ensure the protection of personal data and to demonstrate compliance with this Regulation taking into account the rights and legitimate interests of data subjects and other persons concerned.
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The privacy impact assessment must describe the safeguards and security measures planned to reduce identified risks, protect personal information, and support GDPR compliance while considering affected people's rights and interests.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when a data protection impact assessment is required.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the impact assessment document safeguards, security measures, and other controls planned to address the identified risks and protect personal information and affected people's rights?

sub_obligations.legal_text: Compliance with approved codes of conduct referred to in [Article 40](https://gdpr-info.eu/art-40-gdpr/) by the relevant controllers or processors shall be taken into due account in assessing the impact of the processing operations performed by such controllers or processors, in particular for the purposes of a data protection impact assessment.
sub_obligations.plain_summary: When assessing privacy risks, the organization should take relevant approved privacy codes of conduct into account, especially when preparing a privacy impact assessment.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when a relevant approved Article 40 code of conduct applies to the processing.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Where a relevant approved code of conduct applies, does the impact-assessment process explain how compliance with that code is considered when assessing processing risks?

sub_obligations.legal_text: Where appropriate, the controller shall seek the views of data subjects or their representatives on the intended processing, without prejudice to the protection of commercial or public interests or the security of processing operations.
sub_obligations.plain_summary: When appropriate, the organization should ask affected people or their representatives for their views about planned processing, while protecting legitimate business, public, and security interests.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when seeking the views of affected people or their representatives is appropriate for the planned processing.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy describe a process for seeking the views of affected people or their representatives on planned processing when appropriate?

sub_obligations.legal_text: Where processing pursuant to point (c) or (e) of [Article 6](https://gdpr-info.eu/art-6-gdpr/)(1) has a legal basis in Union law or in the law of the Member State to which the controller is subject, that law regulates the specific processing operation or set of operations in question, and a data protection impact assessment has already been carried out as part of a general impact assessment in the context of the adoption of that legal basis, paragraphs 1 to 7 shall not apply unless Member States deem it to be necessary to carry out such an assessment prior to processing activities.
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The usual impact-assessment requirements may not apply when specific processing is already governed by European or national law and a suitable impact assessment was completed when that law was adopted, unless national law still requires an assessment before processing begins.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when processing relies on Article 6(1)(c) or (e), is specifically regulated by applicable European or national law, and an impact assessment was already completed as part of the law's adoption; the exception does not apply if the relevant Member State requires a new assessment.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: If the organization relies on the Article 35(10) exception, does the policy document the applicable legal basis, the existing general impact assessment, and whether the relevant Member State requires an additional assessment before processing?

sub_obligations.legal_text: Where necessary, the controller shall carry out a review to assess if processing is performed in accordance with the data protection impact assessment at least when there is a change of the risk represented by processing operations.
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The organization must review its processing against the privacy impact assessment when necessary and at least whenever the level of risk changes.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when a data protection impact assessment exists and there is a change in the risk created by the processing, or another circumstance makes a review necessary.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy describe a process for reviewing processing against its impact assessment when necessary and at least whenever the processing risk changes?

article_name: Designation of the data protection officer

sub_obligations.legal_text: the processing is carried out by a public authority or body, except for courts acting in their judicial capacity;
sub_obligations.plain_summary: A public authority or public body generally must appoint a privacy officer, except when a court is processing information as part of its judicial work.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when the organization is a public authority or body; the requirement does not apply to courts acting in their judicial capacity.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: If the organization is a public authority or body, does the policy state whether a privacy officer has been appointed, taking into account the exception for courts acting in their judicial capacity?

sub_obligations.legal_text: the core activities of the controller or the processor consist of processing operations which, by virtue of their nature, their scope and/or their purposes, require regular and systematic monitoring of data subjects on a large scale; or
sub_obligations.plain_summary: A privacy officer must be appointed when the organization's main activities involve large-scale, regular and systematic monitoring of people.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when the organization's core activities involve regular and systematic monitoring of people on a large scale.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: If the organization's main activities involve large-scale, regular and systematic monitoring of people, does the policy identify and designate a privacy officer?

sub_obligations.legal_text: the core activities of the controller or the processor consist of processing on a large scale of special categories of data pursuant to [Article 9](https://gdpr-info.eu/art-9-gdpr/) or personal data relating to criminal convictions and offences referred to in [Article 10](https://gdpr-info.eu/art-10-gdpr/).
sub_obligations.plain_summary: A privacy officer must be appointed when the organization's main activities involve large-scale processing of sensitive information or information about criminal convictions and offences.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when the organization's core activities involve large-scale processing of Article 9 sensitive information or Article 10 criminal-conviction and offence information.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: If the organization's main activities involve large-scale processing of sensitive information or criminal-conviction and offence information, does the policy identify and designate a privacy officer?

sub_obligations.legal_text: A group of undertakings may appoint a single data protection officer provided that a data protection officer is easily accessible from each establishment.
sub_obligations.plain_summary: A group of companies can share one privacy officer as long as that officer can be easily reached from every establishment.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when the organization is part of a group of companies that chooses to use a single privacy officer.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: If the organization is part of a group using one privacy officer, does the policy state how that officer remains easily accessible from each establishment?

sub_obligations.legal_text: Where the controller or the processor is a public authority or body, a single data protection officer may be designated for several such authorities or bodies, taking account of their organisational structure and size.
sub_obligations.plain_summary: Several public authorities or bodies can share one privacy officer when their organizational structure and size make that arrangement appropriate.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when the organization is a public authority or body and shares a privacy officer with other public authorities or bodies.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: If the organization shares a privacy officer with other public authorities or bodies, does the policy explain the arrangement and how organizational structure and size were considered?

sub_obligations.legal_text: In cases other than those referred to in paragraph 1, the controller or processor or associations and other bodies representing categories of controllers or processors may or, where required by Union or Member State law shall, designate a data protection officer.
sub_obligations.plain_summary: Even when appointment is not otherwise mandatory, the organization or a relevant industry association can appoint a privacy officer, and must do so if applicable European or national law requires it.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when none of the mandatory appointment situations in Article 37(1) applies.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: If appointment is not mandatory under Article 37(1), does the policy state whether the organization has voluntarily appointed a privacy officer or whether applicable law requires one?

sub_obligations.legal_text: The data protection officer may act for such associations and other bodies representing controllers or processors.
sub_obligations.plain_summary: A privacy officer can also serve an association or organization that represents groups of organizations responsible for processing information.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when a privacy officer acts for an association or representative body covered by this paragraph.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: If the privacy officer serves an association or representative body, does the policy identify that role and the organizations it covers?

sub_obligations.legal_text: The data protection officer shall be designated on the basis of professional qualities
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The privacy officer must be selected based on suitable professional qualifications and capabilities.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when a privacy officer is designated.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy describe professional qualifications or criteria used when selecting the privacy officer?

sub_obligations.legal_text: and, in particular, expert knowledge of data protection law and practices
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The privacy officer must have expert knowledge of privacy law and practical data-protection matters.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when a privacy officer is designated.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy require the privacy officer to have expert knowledge of privacy law and data-protection practices?

sub_obligations.legal_text: and the ability to fulfil the tasks referred to in [Article 39](https://gdpr-info.eu/art-39-gdpr/).
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The privacy officer must have the ability to carry out the responsibilities assigned under Article 39.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when a privacy officer is designated.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy require the privacy officer to have the skills and ability needed to perform the Article 39 responsibilities?

sub_obligations.legal_text: The data protection officer may be a staff member of the controller or processor, or fulfil the tasks on the basis of a service contract.
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The privacy officer can be an employee or an external professional working under a service contract.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when a privacy officer is designated.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy identify whether the privacy officer is an internal employee or an external professional engaged through a service contract?

sub_obligations.legal_text: The controller or the processor shall publish the contact details of the data protection officer
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The organization must make the privacy officer's contact details publicly available.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when a privacy officer has been designated.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the privacy policy publicly provide the privacy officer's contact details?

sub_obligations.legal_text: and communicate them to the supervisory authority.
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The organization must also give the privacy officer's contact details to the relevant privacy regulator.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when a privacy officer has been designated.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy or compliance procedure state that the privacy officer's contact details are communicated to the relevant supervisory authority?

article_name: Position of the data protection officer

sub_obligations.legal_text: The controller and the processor shall ensure that the data protection officer is involved, properly and in a timely manner, in all issues which relate to the protection of personal data.
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The privacy officer must be involved appropriately and early enough in all matters concerning the protection of personal information.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when a data protection officer has been designated.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy state that the privacy officer must be involved properly and in a timely manner in all matters concerning personal-information protection?

sub_obligations.legal_text: The controller and processor shall support the data protection officer in performing the tasks referred to in [Article 39](https://gdpr-info.eu/art-39-gdpr/) by providing resources necessary to carry out those tasks
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The organization must give the privacy officer the resources needed to perform their responsibilities.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when a data protection officer has been designated.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy describe the resources provided to the privacy officer to perform the responsibilities required by Article 39?

sub_obligations.legal_text: and access to personal data and processing operations
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The privacy officer must have appropriate access to the personal information and processing activities needed to perform their responsibilities.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when a data protection officer has been designated.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy provide the privacy officer with appropriate access to personal information and processing activities needed for their responsibilities?

sub_obligations.legal_text: and to maintain his or her expert knowledge.
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The organization must support the privacy officer in keeping their privacy knowledge and expertise up to date.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when a data protection officer has been designated.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy provide support or resources that allow the privacy officer to maintain and update their expert knowledge?

sub_obligations.legal_text: The controller and processor shall ensure that the data protection officer does not receive any instructions regarding the exercise of those tasks.
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The organization must not direct the privacy officer about how to perform their privacy responsibilities.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when a data protection officer has been designated.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy state that the privacy officer is independent when carrying out their assigned privacy responsibilities and does not receive instructions on how to perform them?

sub_obligations.legal_text: He or she shall not be dismissed or penalised by the controller or the processor for performing his tasks.
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The privacy officer must not be fired or punished for properly carrying out their privacy responsibilities.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when a data protection officer has been designated.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy protect the privacy officer from dismissal or punishment for carrying out their assigned responsibilities?

sub_obligations.legal_text: The data protection officer shall directly report to the highest management level of the controller or the processor.
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The privacy officer must report directly to the organization's highest level of management.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when a data protection officer has been designated.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy state that the privacy officer reports directly to the organization's highest management level?

sub_obligations.legal_text: Data subjects may contact the data protection officer with regard to all issues related to processing of their personal data and to the exercise of their rights under this Regulation.
sub_obligations.plain_summary: People must be able to contact the privacy officer about how their information is used and about exercising their privacy rights.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when a data protection officer has been designated.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy provide a way for people to contact the privacy officer about the use of their personal information and their privacy rights?

sub_obligations.legal_text: The data protection officer shall be bound by secrecy or confidentiality concerning the performance of his or her tasks, in accordance with Union or Member State law.
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The privacy officer must keep information learned while performing their role confidential as required by applicable law.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when a data protection officer has been designated.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy require the privacy officer to maintain secrecy or confidentiality regarding information learned while performing their responsibilities, as required by applicable law?

sub_obligations.legal_text: The data protection officer may fulfil other tasks and duties.
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The privacy officer may perform other responsibilities in addition to their privacy role.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when the privacy officer is assigned additional tasks or duties.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: If the privacy officer has other responsibilities, does the policy identify or permit those additional tasks?

sub_obligations.legal_text: The controller or processor shall ensure that any such tasks and duties do not result in a conflict of interests.
sub_obligations.plain_summary: Any other responsibilities given to the privacy officer must not create a conflict with their privacy role.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when the privacy officer has additional tasks or duties.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy require an assessment or controls to ensure the privacy officer's other responsibilities do not create conflicts of interest?

article_name: Tasks of the data protection officer

sub_obligations.legal_text: to inform and advise the controller or the processor and the employees who carry out processing of their obligations pursuant to this Regulation and to other Union or Member State data protection provisions;
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The privacy officer must inform and advise the organization, its service providers, and staff who handle personal information about their privacy-law responsibilities.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when a data protection officer has been designated.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy assign the privacy officer responsibility for informing and advising management, relevant service providers, and staff about GDPR and other applicable data-protection requirements?

sub_obligations.legal_text: to monitor compliance with this Regulation
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The privacy officer must monitor whether the organization follows GDPR.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when a data protection officer has been designated.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy assign the privacy officer responsibility for monitoring compliance with GDPR?

sub_obligations.legal_text: with other Union or Member State data protection provisions
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The privacy officer must monitor whether the organization follows other applicable European or national privacy requirements.
sub_obligations.applicability_condition: Only when a data protection officer has been designated and other applicable European or national data-protection provisions exist.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy assign the privacy officer responsibility for monitoring compliance with applicable European or national data-protection requirements beyond GDPR?

sub_obligations.legal_text: and with the policies of the controller or processor in relation to the protection of personal data
